title: core-courses
text:
Course Info

    Core General Education  

      Features of the Core General Education Curriculum    

At NCCU, the core general education curriculum is guided by the philosophy of “broad scope and solid foundation.” While establishing students’ fundamental knowledge and skills, it emphasizes the integration and connectivity of knowledge, aiming to reduce fragmentation of learning content.

Moreover, NCCU supports departments participating in core general education teaching through an increased faculty quota system and dedicated course subsidies. These measures help build a university-wide support network for core general education instruction, facilitating the integration of general education with professional training.

                  broad scope & solid foundation                

      Development Direction of General Education    

Since its official implementation in the 2011 academic year, NCCU’s core general education curriculum system has established a distinctive feature of the University’s general education. Over time, the system has undergone adjustments in curriculum structure, subject areas, and credit requirements, with continuous improvements. After more than a decade of implementation, we recognize the need for the general education curriculum to evolve in response to rapid changes in society and the times.

Firstly, the design and positioning of the core general education curriculum need to place greater emphasis on interdisciplinary learning, active practice, and self-directed learning. The curriculum should be designed as interdisciplinary courses that enhance interaction among core general education classes, helping students develop habits of cross-disciplinary learning. Meanwhile, single-subject courses should be classified as Common General Education Courses, distinguishing their roles and highlighting the spirit and value of core general education.

Secondly, NCCU’s current general education tends to focus on cultivating cognitive thinking skills. Moving forward, the curriculum development should prioritize enhancing students’ self-awareness and strengthening learning objectives related to affective domains such as emotion, action, ethics, and values.

Thirdly, general education should establish closer connections with professional education to more effectively support students’ interdisciplinary exploration, facilitating knowledge integration and transformation through diverse learning experiences.

      Talent Cultivation and Social Responsibility    

Cultivating future leaders with penetrating literacy and capabilities is a fundamental responsibility of NCCU. We aspire for our graduates to guide us through an uncertain future. As a hub for knowledge creation and talent development, a university that lacks flexibility in the face of changing times risks losing its promise to the future. Therefore, NCCU must become a sanctuary for talent cultivation that embraces future challenges.

How can a university maintain its influence amid a future full of volatility and uncertainty? How can NCCU uphold its social responsibilities in the rapidly changing 21st century? We believe that breaking down barriers and frameworks to build an open and free university will be NCCU’s long-term development goal.

Within such a learning environment, students receive holistic education, cultivating the competencies of modern citizenship. They develop the practical ability to transform knowledge into action, engage in interdisciplinary learning, and integrate knowledge. This equips them with the skills and vision necessary to face a rapidly evolving and highly uncertain future and to contribute actively to the sustainable development of society.

Course Info

    Core General Education  

      Features of the Core General Education Curriculum    

At NCCU, the core general education curriculum is guided by the philosophy of “broad scope and solid foundation.” While establishing students’ fundamental knowledge and skills, it emphasizes the integration and connectivity of knowledge, aiming to reduce fragmentation of learning content.

Moreover, NCCU supports departments participating in core general education teaching through an increased faculty quota system and dedicated course subsidies. These measures help build a university-wide support network for core general education instruction, facilitating the integration of general education with professional training.

                  broad scope & solid foundation                

      Development Direction of General Education    

Since its official implementation in the 2011 academic year, NCCU’s core general education curriculum system has established a distinctive feature of the University’s general education. Over time, the system has undergone adjustments in curriculum structure, subject areas, and credit requirements, with continuous improvements. After more than a decade of implementation, we recognize the need for the general education curriculum to evolve in response to rapid changes in society and the times.

Firstly, the design and positioning of the core general education curriculum need to place greater emphasis on interdisciplinary learning, active practice, and self-directed learning. The curriculum should be designed as interdisciplinary courses that enhance interaction among core general education classes, helping students develop habits of cross-disciplinary learning. Meanwhile, single-subject courses should be classified as Common General Education Courses, distinguishing their roles and highlighting the spirit and value of core general education.

Secondly, NCCU’s current general education tends to focus on cultivating cognitive thinking skills. Moving forward, the curriculum development should prioritize enhancing students’ self-awareness and strengthening learning objectives related to affective domains such as emotion, action, ethics, and values.

Thirdly, general education should establish closer connections with professional education to more effectively support students’ interdisciplinary exploration, facilitating knowledge integration and transformation through diverse learning experiences.

text:
Regulations

    General Education Credit Transfer and Recognition  

       Regulations for Transferring Credits from Overseas Exchange Programs to General Education Credits at NCCU    

                          01                        
                                            Recognition Principl                    

During their exchange period, undergraduate and graduate students must take at least one course per semester at the host university abroad. After returning, students must submit an official transcript or grade certificate from the overseas university and apply for credit transfer of General Education courses at the NCCU Center for General Education before the one-third point of the following semester.

For transfer of other (specialized) courses, please contact the respective department or offering unit.

                          02                        
                                             Eligibility                    

Undergraduate students officially approved by NCCU for overseas exchange programs may apply to transfer courses taken abroad as General Education credits, based on the similarity between course syllabuses.

                          03                        
                                             Credit Limitations                    

For undergraduate students, the total number of credits transferred from courses taken abroad must not exceed one-third of the minimum graduation credit requirement.

For master’s and doctoral students, the limit is one-half of the minimum graduation credits.

For dual-degree programs, the maximum transferable credits from abroad is one-third of the minimum graduation requirement.

Regarding the conversion of overseas credits to NCCU credits, please refer to Article 8 of the National Chengchi University Student Grade Regulations.

                          04                        
                                             Recognition Principle                    

Principles for Syllabus Review:

Courses with identical titles and content.

Courses with different titles but identical content.

Courses with different titles and content but of the same nature.

Principles for Determining Transferable Credits:

When transferring a course with more credits to a course with fewer credits, the course will be recorded with the lower credit value.

When transferring a course with fewer credits to a course with more credits, the transfer will not be approved, unless the student completes the additional required credits through designated courses assigned by the department or relevant academic units. After completion, the transfer will then be recorded with the lower credit value.

                          05                        
                                            Application Deadline                    

Applications must be submitted before the one-third point of the semester following the exchange:

For the fall semester: around October 18

For the spring semester: around March 28

                          06                        
                                            Important Notes:                    

Applications submitted after the deadline will not be accepted unless special approval is granted through official procedures. Otherwise, the Office of Academic Affairs will mark on the transcript:

“Courses taken during the overseas exchange do not meet course requirements and are not eligible for credit transfer.”

Master’s and doctoral students may apply for recognition, but these credits will not count toward graduation requirements.

                          07                        
                                            Credit Transfer                    

Please refer to Article 8 of the National Chengchi University Guidelines for Student Grade Administration.

                          08                        
                                             Application Procedure                    

Students must apply to transfer courses taken and passed at the overseas university by selecting a similar General Education course offered by NCCU during the semester of exchange. Courses from the past ten years may also be considered. Review will be based on the degree of syllabus similarity.

The following documents must be submitted:

Credit Transfer Application Form

Official transcript from the overseas university, stamped as “True Copy” by the relevant NCCU department or the Office of International Cooperation (OIC)

Syllabus of the course taken abroad (with Chinese or English translation if in a foreign language)

Syllabus of the corresponding NCCU course for which credit transfer is requested

                                             Recognition Principle                    

Students may apply to have courses taken as part of their double major, minor, or credit program recognized as General Education credits in either the Common General or College categories; however, these cannot be recognized as Core General Education credits. Recognition must follow the General Education domain categories approved by the curriculum unit and the General Education domain committee.

                          02                        
                                            Eligibility                    

Students who have completed at least two-thirds of the required credits for their double major or minor, or who have completed credit programs approved according to the University’s [Credit Program Establishment Guidelines](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/download/rulesdata/law09A.pdf).

                                             Credit Limits:                    

Up to 9 credits can be recognized from double major courses.

Up to 6 credits per minor, with a combined maximum of 9 credits for two minors.

Up to 3 credits from credit programs.

The total recognized credits from the above categories cannot exceed 9 credits.

                          04                        
                                            Application Procedure                    

For double majors and minors: Submit the application form to the General Education Center within the application period.

For credit programs: Obtain a signature from the credit program office on the application form, then submit it to the General Education Center within the application period.

                          05                        
                                            Application Deadline                    

Applications must be submitted during the intended graduation semester.

For the fall semester, the deadline is December 30.

For the spring semester, the deadline is May 30.

                          06                        
                                             Important Notes                    

Once approved and recorded, no further changes to recognized courses will be allowed.

If the courses for which recognition is applied are being taken in the current semester, recognition will only be effective after passing the course.

title: ta-eligibility
text:
Guidelines for Applying for Teaching Assistant (TA) Positions

    Teaching Assistant  

      Purpose    

To cultivate students’ independent thinking and analytical abilities, core general education courses differ from regular general education courses. They are three-credit courses, and when conducted through small group discussions, instructors should schedule one hour of group discussion for every two hours of lecture. Discussion times should be included in the course timetable. Through these small group discussion sessions, students can explore interdisciplinary knowledge under the guidance of Teaching Assistants (TAs). The course planning principles are as follows:

 

(1) Course Structure

Core general education courses are conducted with 2 hours of lecture and 1 hour of small group discussion. Flexibility in scheduling is allowed, but the 2:1 ratio must be maintained, and discussion sessions must be included in the timetable. An updated version should be uploaded each semester.

 

(2) Implementation Focus

The main focus of core general education courses is to establish a small group discussion system. TAs should plan discussion topics and teaching materials based on the course community discussions and the syllabus. TAs lead students in small group discussions, encouraging participation, full expression, communication, and critical thinking. Discussions should focus on course topics and not be used for course review or group assignment time.

 

(3) TA Allocation

To implement the small group discussion system, one TA is allocated for every 35 students enrolled. Each TA should divide the students into separate groups and conduct discussions in different spaces. The center will arrange observers to attend and evaluate the discussion sessions.

      Application Procedure    

Instructors should apply for TAs for their class through the TA application platform within the schedule announced by the Academic Affairs Office for the semester. Instructors must upload the course syllabus, specific TA responsibilities, and the TA course plan. Applicants should explain how TA resources will be integrated into the course, detailing each TA’s responsibilities, training methods, and how experience is passed on among TAs.

title: general-knowledge
text:
Course Subsidies  

      Subsidies for Common General Cours    

To encourage instructors to teach and improve general education courses, broaden students’ perspectives, and enhance awareness and social engagement in life education, humanistic care, and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the Center for General Education provides financial support for courses.

 

Eligible Courses:

Common General Education Courses (excluding Core General Education and lecture-type courses) and College General Education Courses (including self-directed learning course).

 

Subsidy Principles:

(a) Courses related to life education, humanistic care, Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and social participation are eligible for a speaker activity subsidy of NT$4,500 per course each semester.

(b) For courses meeting the criteria in (a) with enrollment of 50 or more students, a operational expense subsidy of NT$1,500 per credit per semester will be provided (e.g., NT$3,000 for 2-credit courses, NT$4,500 for 3-credit courses). To promote the incorporation of practical training into courses and to strengthen connections with industry, this subsidy may be reallocated to cover the aforementioned speaker activity fees

(c) Applicants may not apply for this subsidy simultaneously with other funding from the Office of Academic Affairs.

 

Application Period:

From the start of the semester until the end of the semester. For specific dates, please refer to the updated subsidy application form each semester. Once the allocated budget is fully used, the Center reserves the right to stop accepting applications.

 

Application Procedure and Review:

Complete the general education course funding application form and submit it to the Center  for General Education for review.

 

Description of Subsidy Items:

(a) According to National Chengchi University’s regulations on expenditure, the speaker fee for external speakers is capped at NT$4,500 per session. For speakers from the University, the fee is capped at NT$1,600 per session.

(b) Expert attendance fees (limited to external experts) are capped at NT$2,500 per person.

(c) Operational expenses:

Student prize subsidies are capped at NT$500 per person; reimbursement requires attaching scoring criteria and a signed winner list.

Printing costs are capped at NT$1,000.

Other related expenses

The following are not eligible for subsidy: personal use or teaching-related information equipment and books.

(d) Receipts or official invoices must clearly state the purchaser (National Chengchi University or the University’s tax ID 03807654), date, item name, quantity, unit price, and total price, or be accompanied by a detailed signed statement from the handler. Item name, quantity, unit price, and total price may also be supported by related lists. Other funding execution standards follow Ministry of Education and university regulations.

(e) After each activity, all legal expense documents must be submitted for reimbursement by the 5th of the following month (see Attachment 2 in the application instructions).

(f) The deadline for reimbursement follows the Accounting Office regulations; for activities in December, documents must be submitted to the Center for General Education by December 20.

 

Effectiveness Evaluation:

(a) Instructors are required to submit an activity outcome report or performance explanation after the course concludes for record-keeping purposes (see Attachment 3 in the application instructions).

title: core-general-studies
text:
Course Subsidies  

      Core General Courses    

Starting from the 2024–2025 academic year, core general education courses will receive funding support without the need for prior application. Each class will be granted a fixed subsidy of up to NT$4,500 per semester for lecture-related activities, in addition to an administrative expense subsidy of NT$100 per enrolled student (based on the number of students after the add/drop period).

If funding is also received from other sources within the Office of Academic Affairs (such as the Higher Education Sprout Project), instructors may claim only one source of subsidy; duplicate funding is not permitted.

All expenses must be implemented in accordance with the relevant regulations of the Ministry of Education and National Chengchi University. The subsidy items are listed as follows.

 

Subsidy Items:

Funding Limits and Reimbursement Principles:

Lecture Activity Fee:

Each class may receive up to NT$4,500 per semester.

(This subsidy cannot be reallocated to administrative expenses.)

The speaker fee for external speakers is capped at NT$4,500 per session. For speakers from the University, the fee is capped at NT$1,600 per session.

  Expert attendance fees (limited to external experts) are capped at NT$2,500 per person.

Reimbursement must be accompanied by meeting minutes, attendance sheets, or other documentation verifying that the invited scholars or experts participated in the event.

 

Administrative Expense Subsidy:

Based on the number of enrolled students after the add/drop period (excluding withdrawals), a subsidy of NT$100 per student will be provided.

Up to NT$4,500 of the administrative expense subsidy may be reallocated to lecture activity expenses.

The student count does not include intercollegiate course enrollees, auditing students, or AP students.

 

Student awards may account for up to 40% of this budget item (not exceeding NT$4,000 in total), with a maximum of NT$500 per student. Supporting documents such as grading criteria, a signed recipient list, and award descriptions must be attached.

Transportation costs for off-campus visits may be subsidized, primarily for destinations outside the Greater Taipei area.

Final exhibitions or competitions must include evidence of actual implementation, such as an event description, photos, or poster samples.

 Printing expenses are limited to NT$1,000 per class.

 Materials and equipment for laboratory or experimental courses may receive up to NT$5,000 per class; the purpose and content of the experiment must be specified.

The following are not eligible for subsidy: books, items valued above NT$2,000, personal-use or classroom-use IT equipment, and items requiring joint procurement such as toner cartridges and printing paper.

title: model-and-featured-courses
text:
Summer Courses

    Model and Innovative General Education Courses  

      iGER Model and Featured Courses    

Contemporary general education emphasizes not only the breadth of knowledge but also innovation in course design and the practical application of teaching philosophies. This page features exemplary and distinctive general education courses from various universities, showcasing elements such as classroom management, learning space design, pedagogical approaches, and hands-on practices. These examples offer valuable insights and inspiration for instructors seeking to explore the diverse possibilities and pedagogical impact of general education.

The “Featured General Education Courses” invite instructors who have been recognized for excellence in the Ministry of Education’s Teaching Practice Research Program and have completed it three times. The “Model General Education Courses” are presented by recipients of the National Outstanding General Education Teacher Award. These educators share their course design know-how, distinctive features, and the transformation process of their courses, providing valuable references for general education faculty nationwide and enhancing the overall quality of general education.

      Faculty Spotlight    

Department of English – Professor Chih-Hsin Lin: Seeing Both the Trees and the Forest in Core General Education Courses

Professor Chih-Hsin Lin draws on many years of teaching experience in her field to reorganize knowledge and present it in ways that are accessible to students. She was awarded the Ministry of Education’s 11th National Award for Outstanding General Education Teachers.

Her course design emphasizes the principle of “seeing both the trees and the forest.” While guiding students to delve deeply into texts, she also helps them perceive the richness of life within them and cultivate critical thinking skills.

At the same time, Professor Lin places strong emphasis on class preparation and self-directed learning. With the support of teaching assistants, she fosters meaningful interaction between teachers and students. With great passion and patience, she accompanies students in their academic journey, helping them grow through knowledge and making learning a profound and continuous process.

(Excerpted from the Ministry of Education’s publication for the 11th National Award for Outstanding General Education Teachers, p. 30)

title: core-courses-introduction
text:
Course Info

    核心通識課程  

      核心通識課程特色    

政大的核心通識課程以「寬口徑、厚基礎」為理念，在建立學生基礎知能的同時，強調知識的統整性與連結性，並減少知識型態的零碎化。同時，政大透過[增撥員額制度](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/zh/%E6%B3%95%E8%A6%8F-%E8%A1%A8%E5%96%AE/%E6%95%99%E5%8B%99%E8%99%95%E6%B3%95%E8%A6%8F%E8%B3%87%E6%96%99%E5%BA%AB/%E9%80%9A%E8%AD%98%E6%95%99%E8%82%B2%E4%B8%AD%E5%BF%83-1/4410-%E5%9C%8B%E7%AB%8B%E6%94%BF%E6%B2%BB%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%B8%E5%A2%9E%E6%92%A5%E5%93%A1%E9%A1%8D%E7%99%BC%E5%B1%95%E9%80%9A%E8%AD%98%E6%95%99%E8%82%B2%E5%9F%B7%E8%A1%8C%E8%A6%81%E9%BB%9E-2)與[核心通識課程補助辦法](https://gecenter.nccu.edu.tw/faculty-zone/course-subsidy/core-general-studies/)，將資源挹注參與核心通識課程教學的院系所，以建立全校性的核心通識教學支援網，並使通識與專業教育得以融通。

                  寬口徑、厚基礎                

      通識教育發展方向    

政大核心通識課程制度自100學年度正式實施起，已建立政大通識教育的重要特色，這項制度在實施後，也歷經課程架構、領域別與修習學分要求的調整，並持續精進。在現行核心通識課程制度實施十餘年後的今天，我們也看見通識課程在時代的快速變遷下轉型的需要。

 

首先，核心通識課程在設計與定位上，需要更加強調跨領域、行動實踐與自主學習等元素——設計為跨域課程，強化核心通識課程間的交流，讓學生從修習核心通識課程中建立跨域學習的習慣，同時將單一主題的課程歸類為一般通識課，以此建立與一般通識課程的區別與分工，從而凸顯核心通識課程的精神與價值。

第二，目前政大通識教育較偏重於認知思維能力的培養。未來需要將「提升學生自我覺察能力」，強化「情意」、「行動」、「倫理」與「價值」等學習目標作為課程發展的重心。第三，通識教育應與專業教育建立更緊密的連結，以更有效地協助學生進行跨域探索，在多元學習中進行知識統整與轉化。

      人才培育與社會責任    

培育具有穿透性素養與能力的未來領袖，是政大應盡的大學責任，我們期許政大培育的人才，能夠引領我們走向不確定的未來。大學作為知識創造與人才培育的場域，若不能具備時移世變的靈活性，自失去應許未來的機會。因此，我們需要政大成為一所面對未來變局的人才培育殿堂。大學該如何在充滿流動性與不確定性的未來，持續發揮其應有的影響力呢？政大又如何在多變的21世紀，承擔未來社會的責任呢？

我們認為打破藩籬與框架，建構開放而自由的大學，將是政大長期的發展目標。學生在此學習環境中接受全人的陶冶，培養現代公民的素養能力，建立將知識轉化為行動的實踐力，進行跨域的學習並具有統合知識的能力，以具有面對快速變化與高度不確定的未來世界之能力及視野，並進而為社會的永續發展作出積極的貢獻。

title: faculty-zone
text:
核心通識課程審查  

      共同課綱審查    

依據國立政治大學增撥員額發展通識教育執行要點第八點規定，開設核心通識課程單位應每三年檢修其共同課程主軸，並送各領域小組及通識教育委員會審核通過。

      課程審查    

依據國立政治大學增撥員額發展通識教育執行要點第九點規定，核心通識課程應每滿三年接受一次審查，審查相關規劃與指標請依據國立政治大學核心通識課程進退場審查規劃辦理。

      受評單位    

開設核心通識課程之教學單位。

      審查時間    

115學年度開始，每三年同時進行共同課綱及前三年課程審查。

      審查標準    

審查標準共分為下列三大指標：

(1) 開課人學分及選課人學分，並參酌各領域平均數。

(2) 課程教學意見調查及學習成效。

(3) 教師教學社群與課程教學團隊之運作情形。

      審查程序    

(1) 教學單位每三年自行檢核各項指標，並檢具相關佐證資料，經所屬系、所、院課程委員會或相同層級會議同意，於學期結束後送至通識教育中心，同時提送未來三年之共同課綱。

(2)次學期先由領域小組審查，再送通識教育委員會確認是否通過，若未通過則需送外審，外審應遴聘該領域校外委員至少三名，以進行書面審查。

(3) 校外委員審查結果比照大學院系所評鑑標準，分為通過、待觀察、未通 過。除通過之外，應提供審查建議，經相關領域小組及通識教育委員會 確認後，待改善者請教學單位每學年回復執行情形，未通過者，簽請校長同意退場。

text:
Course Info

    通識架構簡介  

 

本校通識課程包括三大類：

第一類為「語文通識」，包括中國語文通識課程與外國語文通識課程。

中國語文通識請見：[中國語文通識課程共同核心綱要](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1-BfpexTlqPK4VbBxnzAB8xwVvd72cBCO/view?usp=sharing)

外國語文通識請見：[外文通識修課架構](https://flc.nccu.edu.tw/zh_tw/course/107CollegeEnglish)

 

第二類為「一般通識」，包括人文學、社會科學、自然科學與資訊四大領域通識課程。

第三類為「書院通識」，包括書院一般通識課程與自主學習課程。

 

自109學年度起入學的學生，在本校需修習28個通識學分（超過不採計）；包括3-6學分之中文通識，6學分之外文通識，一般通識中的人文、社會與自然等三大領域各3-7學分與資訊領域2-3學分（資訊相關學系之學生可免修資訊領域通識課程，詳見「修課規定」）， 以及0-3學分之書院通識。

 

此外，在「一般通識」下規劃「核心通識課程」，以建立學生的基礎核心知識、形塑公民意識、培養宏觀思維、批判思辨與自學能力為目標。

「核心通識課程」為群修課程，本校學生在人文、社會與自然領域需至少修習兩門不同領域之核心通識課程。

title: model-and-featured-courses
text:
Summer Courses

    典範與特色課程  

      iGER典範與特色課程    

當代通識教育不僅關注知識的廣度，更重視課程設計的創新與教學理念的實踐。本頁精選本校與各大學的典範與特色通識課程，涵蓋班級經營、學習空間設計、教學理念與實務等面向，提供授課教師觀摩參考，共同思考通識課程的多元可能與教學啟發。

特色通識課程邀請教育部教學實踐研究計畫績優且執行過三次之教師，典範通識課程則邀請歷屆教育部全國傑出通識教育教師獎得主。由教師分享課程設計know-how、課程特色及課程轉化歷程，以供全國通識教育教師參考，提升整體通識教育品質。

      本校教師專區    

英國語文學系｜林質心老師：讓核心通識課程見樹又見林

林質心老師老師運用多年專業系所的教學經驗，將知識重新梳理並以學生易懂的方式傳授。曾榮獲教育部第十一屆全國傑出通識教師獎。

老師的課程設計強調「見樹又見林」，在深入文本時，引導學生從文本中感知生命的厚度，並培養批判思考的能力。

同時，質心老師十分重視課前預習和學生自學，並透過教學助理的協助，促進師生間的互動，她以高度的熱情與耐心陪伴學生，幫助學生在知識中成長，讓學習成為深刻且持續的過程。(擷取自《教育部第十一屆全國傑出通識教育教師獎得獎人專輯》，頁30）

本校專訪報導：[知識脈絡連結生命經驗　林質心榮獲全國傑出通識教育教師獎](https://www.nccu.edu.tw/p/404-1000-18634.php?Lang=zh-tw#gsc.tab=0)

本校專訪報導：[政大首位傑出通識教育教師　英文系副教授林質心：歸功於團隊合作](https://www.nccu.edu.tw/p/404-1000-17285.php?Lang=zh-tw#gsc.tab=0)

title: independent-study
text:
Course Info

    Independent Study  

為培養學生自主學習、問題解決及跨領域實務等綜合能力，在書院通識領域規劃自主學習課程，提供學生主動發展課程之機會，建立師生共校文化，依申請分為方式「開課型」及「認證型」二類自主學習。

 

自主學習（Self-Directed Learning）不只是「自己讀書」，而是一個有目標、有計畫、有反思的循環過程。

 

在開始之前，問自己四個問題：

為什麼想學這個？（內在動機越強，越容易堅持）

我想達到什麼程度？（初學者、能實際應用、還是成為專家？）

我預計投入多少時間？

我是否具有自主學習的先備知識與能力？

若尚未具有自主學習的先備能力我們推薦的相關課程：

1.跨界實驗室（下學期開課）

2.跨界專題－Ｘ計畫（下學期開課）

3.尋找心中的創業家（上學期開課）

4.人生設計、設計人生（上學期開課）

5.新生專題：自學力（大一上開課）22

 

每學期申請截止日期請注意首頁最新消息公告。

 

走在自主學習的路上，我們都是伙伴。

這個過程會依狀況滾動式修正，讓我們一起在政大建立起自主學習的制度！

text:
Course Info

    自主學習  

為培養學生自主學習、問題解決及跨領域實務等綜合能力，在書院通識領域規劃自主學習課程，提供學生主動發展課程之機會，建立師生共校文化，依申請分為方式「開課型」及「認證型」二類自主學習。

 

自主學習（Self-Directed Learning）不只是「自己讀書」，而是一個有目標、有計畫、有反思的循環過程。

 

在開始之前，問自己四個問題：

為什麼想學這個？（內在動機越強，越容易堅持）

我想達到什麼程度？（初學者、能實際應用、還是成為專家？）

我預計投入多少時間？

我是否具有自主學習的先備知識與能力？

若尚未具有自主學習的先備能力我們推薦的相關課程：

1.跨界實驗室（下學期開課）

2.跨界專題－Ｘ計畫（下學期開課）

3.尋找心中的創業家（上學期開課）

4.人生設計、設計人生（上學期開課）

5.新生專題：自學力（大一上開課）

 

每學期申請截止日期請注意首頁最新消息公告。

 

走在自主學習的路上，我們都是伙伴。

這個過程會依狀況滾動式修正，讓我們一起在政大建立起自主學習的制度！

text:
課程補助  

      核心通識    

自113學年度起，核心通識課程經費補助毋須事先申請，每班每學期固定補助演講活動費至多4500元，另依(加簽暨退課後)選課人數補助每人次100元業務費。

 

如獲教務處其他經費補助([如教務處高教深耕計畫](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/zh/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=5240))，請擇一領取，不重複補助。

 

各項經費執行標準悉依教育部及[本校相關規定辦理](http://www.acc.nccu.edu.tw/content/%E6%A0%A1%E5%85%A7%E8%A6%8F%E5%AE%9A)，補助項目如下。

 

補助項目

上限及補助原則

演講活動費 每班4,500元 (不得流用至業務費)

  演講費外聘最高每場次4,500元，內聘最高每場次1,600元。

 出席費(限外聘)每位每場次以2,500元為上限。報支應有會議紀錄、簽到表或足  資證明學者專家親自參與會議之文件。

依加簽既退課之後選課人數(不含棄修)補助每人次100元業務費。

(業務費最高可流用4,500元至前項演講活動費)

(人次計算不包含校際選課、隨班附讀、AP)

 學生獎品以本項費用40%為上限(且不得超過4,000元)，每位最高 500 元，核銷 時請附上評分標準、得獎者簽收名單及得獎品項。

 校外參訪交通費。以補助大台北以外地區為原則。

 期末展演或競賽應有舉辦之事實，應檢附活動說明、照片、海報樣張等。

 影印費以 1,000 元為上限。

 實驗課程教材/實驗器具每班上限5,000元，並敘明實驗用途及內容。

 以下各項不予補助：書籍、2,000元以上之物品、個人使用或教學場域所需之資 訊相關物品、應採共約之碳粉匣及影印紙等。

title: certification-based-self-directed-learning
text:
Course Info

    Independent Study  

To develop distinctive College General Education Courses and cultivate students’ comprehensive abilities in self-directed learning, problem-solving, and interdisciplinary practice, the College General Education Domain offers Self-directed Learning courses. These courses provide students with opportunities to proactively plan and develop their own learning paths, fostering a collaborative campus culture of shared learning between teachers and students.

Self-directed Learning is divided into two categories based on the application process: “Course-based” and “Certification-based” types.

For detailed information, please visit

[Relevant Regulations](https://gecenter.nccu.edu.tw/en/student-zone/gec-credit-waiver/relevant-regulations/)

[Course-based Self-Directed Learning](https://gecenter.nccu.edu.tw/independent-study/course-based/)

[Certification-based Self-Directed Learning](https://gecenter.nccu.edu.tw/en/independent-study/certification-based-self-directed-learning/)

[Achievements over the years](https://gecenter.nccu.edu.tw/independent-study/achievements-over-the-years/)

Course-based Self-Directed Learning 

Starting from the Spring semester of the 2020 academic year, NCCU implemented the Course-Based Self-directed Learning system.

Class-based self-directed learning courses are courses where the content and learning approach are designed by students alone or jointly developed by faculty and Full-time and part-time faculty members or eligible full-time researchers of the university may teach or supervise these courses. Proposals involving certificate-based courses, courses already offered by the University, or repeated submissions of similar courses for a third time shall not be accepted.

 

Course title and credits

The course title shall be “Self-Directed Learning Project: [Learning Topic].” The course period is one semester in principle, with credits ranging from one to two credits.

 

Application

One or more undergraduate students at NCCU should submit a self-directed learning plan and relevant application documents as announced by the Center of General Education (hereinafter referred as “the Center”). Proposers shall possess the prerequisite knowledge for self-directed learning, attend the course in its entirety, and be responsible for the course implementation and the submission of a final report. Failure to fulfill any of these requirements without just cause will result in disqualification from submitting proposals for a period of two years.

 

Review Process

The self-directed learning proposal must first be reviewed by the Center, and then evaluated by the College General Education Domain Review Committee. The course will only be offered upon approval by both the General Education Committee and the Academic Affairs Council.

 

Hourly lecture fee and funding sources

The course budget shall be capped at the product of the hourly pay rate for professors, the number of credits, and the number of instructional weeks. Funding may come from government subsidies or the University’s self-generated revenue. Duplicate applications for other subsidies from the Office of Academic Affairs are not permitted.

In accordance with Ministry of Education regulations, instructors shall be compensated based on their actual teaching hours. Since these courses fall outside the regular degree programs, the teaching hours shall not count toward the full-time faculty member’s official teaching load for the academic year.

 

Instructors are responsible for the overall management of the course and the assessment of student performance. If the actual teaching hours are less than half of the total scheduled hours, the instructor may instead be compensated at the rate applicable for supervising a master’s thesis.

 

[Self-study course application form](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1g0Gg_dhsQGDUuE82rfucffJM02lSRVc6/view?usp=sharing)

[Self-Directed Learning College Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/cccollege2016/?locale=zh_TW)

 2. 我想達到什麼程度？（初學者、能實際應用、還是成為專家？）

 3. 我預計投入多少時間？

 4. 我是否具有自主學習的先備知識與能力？

 

若尚未具有自主學習的先備能力，我們推薦相關課程：

 1. 跨界實驗室（下學期開課）

 2. 跨界專題－Ｘ計畫（下學期開課）

 3. 尋找心中的創業家（上學期開課）

 4. 人生設計、設計人生（上學期開課）

 5. 新生專題：自學力（大一上開課）

 

每學期申請截止日期請注意首頁最新消息公告。

 

走在自主學習的路上，我們都是伙伴。

這個過程會依狀況滾動式修正，讓我們一起在政大建立起自主學習的制度！

 

欲瞭解詳細說明，請至 

[法規](https://drive.google.com/file/d/11dCdOibhTktvbkJr_a28-WhL9FEN6yIw/view?usp=drive_link)

[開課型](https://gecenter.nccu.edu.tw/independent-study/course-based/)

[認證型](https://gecenter.nccu.edu.tw/independent-study/certification-based-self-directed-learning/)

[歷年成果](https://gecenter.nccu.edu.tw/independent-study/achievements-over-the-years/)

開課型自主學習 

從109學年第2學期起，政大開始實施開課型自主學習課程製度。

開課型自主學習課程係指學習內容與方式由學生自主規劃，或師生共同規劃設計之課程，得由本校專職兼任教師或具教師資格之專任研究人員授課或指導。證明類課程、校內已有相關課程、課程重複提案次均不予受理。

 

課程名稱及學分

課程名稱為「自主學習專題：○○○（學習主題）」，學習時程以一學期為原則，學分數為一至二學分。

申請

本校學生班在學學生一人以上，依通知識教育中心（以下簡稱本中心）公告事項，檢具自主學習計畫及相關申請文件。提案人應有自主學習先備知識，並全程修課，負責課程運作及期末成果報告，若無故未能滿足以上要求，二年內不得再提出申請。

審查

自主學習計畫書須經本中心審查後提送書院教育領域小組評審，再經通知識教育委員會及教務會議通過後開課。

鐘點計算與底座來源

課程預算上限以教授授課鐘點費乘以學分數乘上課週數計，相關事宜取決於政府補助款或本校自籌收入支應。不得重複申請教務處其他補助。

授課教師依教育部規定及實際授課時數繳納鐘點費，屬學制外授課，不納入專任教師當學年授課時數內計算。

開課教師應負責課程經營與成績評定，實際授課時數低於一半者，得支領以碩士班論文指導費為支領標準之課程指導費。

認證型自主學習 

為鼓勵學生自主發展、解決問題和創新實踐能力，自112學每年起實施認證型自主學習學分申請。

認證型自主學習分為「學術探索」、「行動實踐」與「創新實踐作」三大類別，學生除經校內教師輔導或獨立完成學習計畫申請後自主學習學習分認證，並由參加校外政府、民間企業舉辦的專題實習或志願者等計劃（非課程要求）執行自主學習計畫學習，學生預先填寫線上表格送交作業表，不限時程（學期中或寒暑假皆可）、場域，於完成後申請自主學習認證作業學分，亦可七人（含）以上申請團體認證，成績以「通過／不通過」考評。學分以學分一學分為基本單位，採計上限二學分。

學生完成計畫後，畢業前於各學期申請期限前，提交交學習檔案、回饋單、成果報告等相關資料，並於書院教育小組審查中進行，若獲通過會議相關學院通識學分，所得成績單及畢業學分計算。

title: review-of-core-general-education-courses
text:
核心通識課程審查  

      共同課綱審查    

依據國立政治大學增撥員額發展通識教育執行要點第八點規定，開設核心通識課程單位應每三年檢修其共同課程主軸，並送各領域小組及通識教育委員會審核通過。

      課程審查    

依據國立政治大學增撥員額發展通識教育執行要點第九點規定，核心通識課程應每滿三年接受一次審查，審查相關規劃與指標請依據國立政治大學核心通識課程進退場審查規劃辦理。

      受評單位    

開設核心通識課程之教學單位。

      審查時間    

115學年度開始，每三年同時進行共同課綱及前三年課程審查。

      審查標準    

審查標準共分為下列三大指標：

(1) 開課人學分及選課人學分，並參酌各領域平均數。

(2) 課程教學意見調查及學習成效。

(3) 教師教學社群與課程教學團隊之運作情形。

      審查程序    

(1) 教學單位每三年自行檢核各項指標，並檢具相關佐證資料，經所屬系、所、院課程委員會或相同層級會議同意，於學期結束後送至通識教育中心，同時提送未來三年之共同課綱。

(2)次學期先由領域小組審查，再送通識教育委員會確認是否通過，若未通過則需送外審，外審應遴聘該領域校外委員至少三名，以進行書面審查。

(3) 校外委員審查結果比照大學院系所評鑑標準，分為通過、待觀察、未通 過。除通過之外，應提供審查建議，經相關領域小組及通識教育委員會 確認後，待改善者請教學單位每學年回復執行情形，未通過者，簽請校長同意退場。

      核心通識課程進退場審查檢核表

title: application-for-general-education-course-inclusion
text:
申請通識學分認定  

教務處通識教育中心（以下簡稱通識中心）為鼓勵學生多元跨域學習，辦理學生修讀雙主修、輔系及學分學程課程學分認定為通識教育學分作業。各開課單位若同意修讀雙主修、輔系、學分學程學生得據此辦理通識學分認定，請填具[認定通識領域類別調查表](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1b0xRA32xEf60ZSEA6OiI2qOM5Og7nkjr/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=115073937196292235953&rtpof=true&sd=true)，送交通識中心各領域承辦人，提案每學期通識領域小組會議、通識教育委員會議及教務會議審議通過後，由通識中心上網公告，即完成通識學分認定申請。

      申請認定說明    

 

一、教務處業於108 學年度第2學期臨時教務會議通過「國立政治大學通識教育學分認定作業要點」，有以下重點：

 

(一) 學生修讀雙主修、輔系以及學分學程課程者，得提出申請並經審核通過，將其修讀之雙主修、輔系以及學分學程課程認定為一般通識教育學分，但不得認定為核心通識。

(二) 雙主修認定以九學分為上限，每一輔系認定以六學分為上限、二輔系學分合計認定以九學分為上限；學分學程課程認定以三學分為上限。以上認定合計以九學分為上限。

(三)學生應檢附申請表件，送通識中心審核可認定領域及學分數，再送教務處註冊組審核通過後，方完成認定。惟申請學分學程認定通識學分者，須先經學程開設單位確定其修習資格及課程係屬學程所列修習科目。

 

二、通識中心本於專業領域認定精神，強化跨域學習成效，請辦理雙主修、輔系及學分學程之開課單位填覆申請認定的通識領域別。雙主修、輔系及學位學程可申請單一領域或跨領域別認定，惟資訊領域限定為必、群修且具備程式設計事實之課程；學分學程請以課程為單位，逐一填寫擬認定之通識領域別。經公告後不得輕易變動，若有課程異動，請通知通識中心並重新申請認定。

三、各單位填具之領域認定調查表，後續提送各領域小組委員審議，並提通識教育委員會議及教務會議核備後公告之。

四、學分學程請提供學程之修習科目一覽表，俾利後續審議。

(三)自然科學領域：張小姐，分機62847，信箱：[changwc@nccu.edu.tw](mailto:changwc@nccu.edu.tw)

(四)資訊領域：林小姐，分機62857，信箱：[jeanlin@nccu.edu.tw](https://gecenter.nccu.edu.tw/114-2%e9%80%9a%e8%ad%98%e8%aa%b2%e7%a8%8b%e9%96%8b%e8%aa%b2%e5%8f%8a%e7%95%b0%e5%8b%95%e7%94%b3%e8%ab%8b%e8%87%b309-26%e6%88%aa%e6%ad%a2/jeanlin@nccu.edu.tw)

Regulations

    通識學分認抵  

      雙主修、輔系及學分學程認定通識學分    

                          01                        
                                            認定原則                    

學生得將其修讀之雙主修、輔系、學分學程課程提出申請認定為一般或書院通識學分，但不得認定為核心通識學分。學生應依開課單位提送通識領域小組會議審議通過之領域別，經通識教育中心審查，認定為通識學分。

[雙主修、輔系認定通識領域類別](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1NrM_gKNjUxEYvU-kK_0LmX32mhfVlMNJ/view?usp=sharing)

[學分學程認定領域類別](https://drive.google.com/file/d/10f1w4dlQTNqgQFFeRYh9HsX1Io9H3gfL/view?usp=sharing)

[免修資訊領域通識學系（組）之雙主修、輔系修讀學生可申請認定資訊領域通識學分科目一覽表](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1dx0vkio6mw4aAl8rA2e5WigoDu-_VrC6/view?usp=sharing)

                          02                        
                                            申請資格                    

修習雙主修、輔系學分達學系規定學分三分之二以上者，或修習依據本校「[學分學程設置辦法](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/download/rulesdata/law09A.pdf)」通過之學分學程者。

                          03                        
                                            學分規定                    

雙主修認定以9學分為上限，每一輔系認定以6學分為上限、二輔系學分合計認定以9學分為上限；學分學程課程認定以3學分為上限。上述學分認定以9學分為上限。

                          04                        
                                            辦理期間                    

依據學校行事曆所訂學期三分之二基準日前提出申請。申請後不可變更，建議學生預定畢業當學期提出申請。

                          05                        
                                            申請流程                    

雙主修、輔系—於辦理期間至通識中心遞交申請表。

學分學程—先由學程辦公室在申請表上「學程辦公室核章」處核章，再於辦理期間至通識中心遞交申請表。經通識中心通過審查，再檢附申請表送件至教務處註冊組審核通過後，方完成認定。

                          06                        
                                            注意事項                    

認定科目經核定認定並登錄後，不得再進行其他變更申請。

申請認定課程如為當學期修課者，俟該科成績及格後始生認定效力。

建議同學於畢業當學期加退選前，提前確認相關規定與學分數是否足夠，以免影響畢業資格。

    開課申請  

      開課規定    

開設通識課程應符合下列原則：

一、單學期每門以二學分為原則。若課程規劃具備小組討論等活動，則每門以三學分為原則。

二、一般通識開課人數設定不得低於50人。核心通識以上限140人為原則。(語文通識與校際合開通識課程不在此限)

三、不得設定先修課程。

四、得設定排除修讀學系。一般通識以排除相關學系、院學生為原則，核心通識應排除與其課程學習相關之本系、雙修與輔系學生。如有特殊情況，應敘明理由。

五、除核心通識之外，通識課程同一科目每學期以開設一班為原則，增班應提通識教育委員會審議。(語文通識與校際合開通識課程不在此限)

六、得設計跨領域課程，學分採認僅限單一領域。

七、應依本校規定之時段及科目數開課。(語文通識與校際合開通識課程不在此限)

八、核心通識課程應開設三學分，以小組討論方式進行時，教師每授課二小時應安排小組討論一小時，並將討論課時間排入課表，得採計為教師授課時數三小時。

各類教學助理(TA)依本校教學助理制度實施辦法及相關規定提出申請，審查通過後核配。

九、通識課程應與專業課程區隔，不得合開或輪開。

title: faq
text:
FAQ

    常見問題  

 

學生 常見問題
 

通識學分認定
 

Q

          為何會建議在畢業當學期再申請通識學分認定？不能提前申請嗎？        

展開
收合

 

A

因為一旦申請便不能再更動，為保障同學權益，建議於畢業當學期確認所有學分規劃後再申請。

Q

          我預計延畢一學期／一年去國內／外交換，可以事先申請雙主修／輔系／學分學程學分認定嗎？        

展開
收合

 

A

建議回校／回國再申請，或委託他人幫忙申請。委託他人申請時，須檢附「[國立政治大學教務處註冊組各項證明文件申辦委託書](https://diplomacy.nccu.edu.tw/upload/28/doc/3092/44_3372%20(1).pdf)」。

Q

          雙主修、輔系與學分學程課程中，哪些課程可以進行認定？        

展開
收合

 

A

請檢視雙主修、輔系或學分學程的必修課目表，並以表上的課程進行認定。

[雙主修/輔系必修科目查詢](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/zh/%E6%9C%8D%E5%8B%99%E9%A0%85%E7%9B%AE/%E8%AA%B2%E7%A8%8B%E7%9B%B8%E9%97%9C%E8%B3%87%E8%A8%8A/%E5%BF%85%E4%BF%AE%E7%A7%91%E7%9B%AE%E8%A1%A8%E6%9F%A5%E8%A9%A22)

Q

          要怎麼判斷課程能夠認定哪個通識領域？        

展開
收合

 

A

請見「雙主修、輔系認定通識領域類別」、「學分學程認定領域類別」、「免修資訊領域通視學系（組）之雙主修、輔系修讀學生可申請認定資訊領域通識學分科目一覽表」。表單上沒有出現的系、學分學程、課程，即表示無法申請認定。

[雙主修、輔系認定領域類別](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1NrM_gKNjUxEYvU-kK_0LmX32mhfVlMNJ/view?usp=sharing)

[學分學程認定領域類別](https://drive.google.com/file/d/14B38rV3HuVdGHjOswqZWiNT2tf8nzqya/view?usp=sharing)

[國立政治大學通識課程架構表](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1E2_30xjfljzYmbUVuXdgs8IcaMEq6UBh/view?usp=sharing)

Q

          我用雙主修、輔系與學分學程的課程進行認定，那我本來算在必選修的學分會不會被扣掉，進而影響我的主修、輔系與學分學程資格？        

展開
收合

 

A

不會，用以認抵學分之雙主修、輔系與學分學程課程在畢業學分計算上將被視為通識學分，但不影響雙主修、輔系與學分學程之身分認定與學位取得。

有修讀雙主修、輔系與學分學程規定之科目學分即具備資格，只是申請認定的課程學分類別會由專業改為通識，也請務必確認畢業學分數中的專業必選修學分數是否足夠。

Q

          申請時要注意哪些事情？        

展開
收合

 

A

一、由於申請後無法更動，強烈建議於預定畢業當學期申請。

二、請先確認已取得的通識各領域學分數，確認修習的雙主修、輔系、學分學程可認定的領域類別後，上網下載或親至本中心填寫申請表後辦理。

三、認定科目經核定並登錄後，不得再進行其他變更申請。

 

轉系、雙主修轉主系
 

Q

          我轉系/雙主修或輔系後，發現已修過的通識課排除轉系/雙主修或輔系的學生選修，這樣還可以計入我的畢業通識學分嗎？轉系至免修資訊通識的學系，已修習的資訊通識學分還可以計入畢業學分嗎？        

展開
收合

 

A

根據[本校學生修讀雙主修、輔系辦法](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/download/rulesdata/law12A.pdf)第六條：學生於取得雙主修或輔系修讀資格前所選修之通識科目，雖為雙主修或輔系排除修讀，仍採計為畢業通識科目學分。已修習的資訊通識學分會保留，可計入畢業學分。反之，若從免修資訊通識的學系轉至需修習的學系，則需補足應修學分。

Q

          關於各類組合認定學分上限，我有修輔系還有學分學程，這樣可以認定多少通識學分？        

展開
收合

 

A

全部可認定學分合計以9學分為上限，請參考[國立政治大學通識教育學分認定作業要點](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/images/download/rulesdata/law117A.pdf)。

Q

          我本來是A系，後來雙主修B系並預計自B系畢業，本系轉為輔系，我可以如何申請通識學分認定？        

展開
收合

 

A

需先至註冊組申請「雙主修轉主系」，再以原本的A系（現為輔系）課程進行通識學分認定。請注意若欲將本系轉為輔系，一樣需滿足輔系學分達學系規定三分之二以上之規定，方能申請。詳細規定請參本校[學生修讀雙主修、輔系辦法。](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/download/rulesdata/law12A.pdf)

Q

          我本來是A系，後來轉系至B系並預計於B系畢業，我可以用A系的必修抵為通識課學分嗎？        

展開
收合

 

A

不行。若你希望用A系必修抵為通識課學分，就需要申請將A系作為雙主修或輔系，再檢視[雙主修、輔系必修課目表](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/zh/%E8%AA%B2%E5%8B%99%E7%B5%84/%E8%AA%B2%E7%A8%8B%E8%B3%87%E8%A8%8A)與[雙主修、輔系認定通識領域類別](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/DB/upload/%E8%AA%8D%E5%AE%9A%E9%A0%98%E5%9F%9F%E9%A1%9E%E5%88%A5.pdf)，以表上的必選修課程進行相對應的通識學分認定。

 

國內外交換抵免一般通識
 

Q

          我在國內交換學校修習的課程可以用來抵免通識學分嗎？哪些課程可以抵免？        

展開
收合

 

A

通識抵免以交換學校所修習之通識課程為限。詳細規定請見《[國立政治大學學生抵免學分辦法](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/download/rulesdata/law06A.pdf)》。

Q

          國外學分要怎麼抵免通識學分？上限是多少？        

展開
收合

 

A

欲抵免通識學分之課程由通識中心審查，專業課程則由專業系所審查。關於抵免學分限制，學士班以不超過畢業最低學分總數三分之一為限；博、碩士班以不超過畢業最低學分總數二分之一為限；出國修讀雙聯學位學分抵免以不超過畢業最低學分數總數三分之二為限。詳細規定請見《[國立政治大學出國選修課程實施辦法](https://oic.nccu.edu.tw/Upload/FileManager/4fd69618-9214-4e09-8d0d-fedd22618293.pdf)》。

 

Q

          國外學分抵免一定要回國才能辦理嗎？我可以在出國前先確認國外學分是否能夠成功抵免嗎？        

展開
收合

 

A

由於抵免審查是根據國外課程與政大一般通識課程的課綱相似度進行審查，因此無法在出國前確認是否可以成功抵免。若同學欲事先確認國外課程是否能夠抵免，可以在國外交換選課期間以電子郵件方式向通識中心確認，來信時請附上「欲抵免之政大一般通識課程課綱」與「與政大一般通識課程內容相似之國外學校課程大綱」，以利通識中心進行事前審查。

若事前審查結果為「可以抵免」，同學仍需於交換期間修習該科目成績及格，並於事後正式申請時檢附成績單及相關文件，始可抵免。

詳細申請流程請見「[國外交換學分認抵本校一般通識學分](https://gecenter.nccu.edu.tw/student-zone/gec-credit-waiver/credits-from-overseas-exchange-programs/)」。

Q

          我在國內/外交換，可以把交換學校所修的課拿來抵免為本校通識學分嗎？        

展開
收合

 

A

依據[國立政治大學學生出國選修課程實施辦法](https://oic.nccu.edu.tw/Upload/FileManager/4fd69618-9214-4e09-8d0d-fedd22618293.pdf)，你可以在交換學期結束後，提出交換學校所修習之正式成績單或成績證明書，於次學期三分之一基準日前辦理學分抵免申請。你需要在課程查詢系統內找到本校「名稱或課綱相同或相近」的一般通識課程（核心與書院通識皆不可拿來認抵）。課程條件以交換當學期開設為主、但交換該年度算起十年內的通識課程皆可。抵免科目及學分數請參考本校[學生抵免學分辦法](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/images/download/rulesdata/law06A.pdf)第六條。提出申請後，經通識教育中心審查通過者，即可將交換學校所修課程抵免為本校一般通識學分。

Q

          申請國內外交換抵免通識，流程為何？        

展開
收合

 

A

一、根據國外學校課綱，於本校課程查詢系統搜尋與本校「名稱或課綱相同或相近」的一般通識課程。審查時將以課綱相似度判斷。

二、準備國外成績單影本（需至國合處或系辦加蓋「與正本相符」印章）、欲申請抵免之交換學校課程課綱、對應之政大課程課綱，並於辦理期間內攜申請表至通識中心辦理。

詳細規定與流程，請參考[「國外交換學分認抵本校一般通識學分」頁面](https://gecenter.nccu.edu.tw/student-zone/gec-credit-waiver/credits-from-overseas-exchange-programs/)以及[國立政治大學學生抵免學分辦法](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/images/download/rulesdata/law06A.pdf)。

 

寒/暑期通識課程
 

Q

          暑修課程有哪些？        

展開
收合

 

A

除了學校會因應同學需求開設暑修通識課程之外（時程與詳細規定請見[教務處網頁](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/zh/%E8%A8%BB%E5%86%8A%E7%B5%84/%E6%9A%91%E4%BF%AE%E8%A8%8A%E6%81%AF)或洽註冊組詢問），「全國夏季學院」課程亦可供政大同學於暑期選修，部分課程得認定為通識學分。

學生需遵照「夏季學院通識教育課程實施要點及報名須知」進行選課作業，學費自付（大一新生與學士班學生享有夥伴學校優惠，碩博士生則無），而成績登錄作業則依本校暑修課程規定實施。

Q

          選修寒/暑期通識的資格為何？        

展開
收合

 

A

需為政大在學生，方能修習暑期通識課程。即將入學之大一新生也可憑錄取證明，選修全國夏季學院與SOS暑期線上學院課程，但需於當年10/30前至通識中心申請抵免；同意抵免的課程只登錄科目名稱及學分，不會登錄成績。

Q

          政大認定全國夏季學院的通識學分上限是多少？        

展開
收合

 

A

依據學校選課規定，認定上限為6學分，每學期重新計算。

Q

          我還差兩學分某領域通識就能畢業，可以修暑修通識並申請認定嗎？        

展開
收合

 

A

可以，學校暑修請至見Q14說明並洽註冊組詢問，若選擇全國夏季學院、SOS暑期線上學院，請至官網的「政大」認抵頁面查詢你能選擇的課程，並於辦理期間完成選課、繳費、修課，並向本中心申請學分認定。

Q

          我出於興趣想修課，不想申請學分認定，這樣是否就可以選擇非政大認定的課程？        

展開
收合

 

A

是的，但請注意若選擇非政大認定課程，就不會登記成績。

Q

          我現在休學，可以報名暑修通識嗎？        

展開
收合

 

A

不行喔，要先復學，有在學證明才能至網站完成註冊程序，並進行後續選課、繳費與修課流程。

全國夏季學院官網：[https://www.n2.org.tw/](https://www.n2.org.tw/)

SOS暑期線上學院官網：[https://www.ewant.org/local/enterprise/collegepage.php?id=5](https://www.ewant.org/local/enterprise/collegepage.php?id=5)

通識中心暑期通識懶人包：[https://www.facebook.com/photo?fbid=1061207776056865&set=pcb.1061212512723058](https://www.facebook.com/photo?fbid=1061207776056865&set=pcb.1061212512723058)

詳細規定請洽通識中心承辦人張小姐（校內分機63871）

Q

          通識課程成績如何計算？會影響我的GPA和排名嗎？        

展開
收合

 

A

成績會登錄於該學年度第三學期（校內暑修）或第四學期（全國夏季學院），列入不列入第一、二學期的GPA計算，不影響成績平均，但會影響畢業成績平均排名。

 

其他問題
 

Q

          若我畢業前才發現缺少通識學分該如何補救？        

展開
收合

 

A

請先確認缺少的通識領域學分數，若有修習雙主修、輔系與學分學程且仍具備修習資格，視課程可認定的通識領域是否相符，辦理通識學分認定；若領域不符或不具備前述資格，可報名暑期課程，包括：本校開設之暑修課程（詳細規定請參考[學士班暑期開班選課作業流程](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/download/flowProcess/file/register/register17.pdf)或洽註冊組詢問）、校際暑期通識課程（例如：SOS！暑期線上學院、全國夏季學院，經本校認抵之課程），詳情請見[暑期課程](https://gecenter.nccu.edu.tw/student-zone/summer-courses/)。

Q

          跨領域通識可否一魚二吃，認定為兩個領域學分數？        

展開
收合

 

A

跨領域通識僅可認定為單一領域之學分數，在學期間的成績系統上，會在二領域中隨機顯示其中一個領域，而畢業時原則上將認定為相對學分數較少之領域的學分數。例如：同學修讀跨社會與人文領域之A通識課程，A課程於同學在學期間可能會顯示為「人文領域」或「社會領域」，計算畢業學分時，若同學的社會領域通識學分少於人文領域通識學分，A課程將會被認定為社會領域通識學分。如有需要異動認定領域，請洽[註冊組](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/zh/%E9%97%9C%E6%96%BC%E6%9C%AC%E8%99%95/%E8%A8%BB%E5%86%8A%E7%B5%84?view=default)。

Q

          如何申請抵免中文通識或外文通識學分？        

展開
收合

 

A

中文通識請洽詢[中文系](https://chinese.nccu.edu.tw/PageStaffing?fid=2962)，外文通識請洽[外文中心](https://flc.nccu.edu.tw/zh_tw/About/Administrative)。

 

教師 常見問題
 

開課問題
 

Q

          開設通識課程是否有相關資源挹助，例如：教學助理、經費？        

展開
收合

 

A

目前僅有核心通識課程有提供教學助理及課程經費，其他一般通識課程視課程屬性與修課人數，可向通識中心申請經費補助，自主學習書院通識課程則有對應之補助。另課程若符合教務處教學創新補助課程類別，亦可向承辦單位提出申請。惟當學期若已獲其他機關或單位補助者，不得重複申請。

詳情請見[課程補助](https://gecenter.nccu.edu.tw/faculty-zone/course-subsidy/)

Q

          怎樣的課程需要重新送審？        

展開
收合

 

A

1. 課程異動，包括：新增/變更授課師資、新增/變更開課單位、新增班次、修改排除學系、變更課程名稱、變更課程大綱、變更學分數。

2. 三年以上未開設同一通識課程者。但開設核心通識課程者，不在此限。

Q

          如何申請開設通識課程？        

展開
收合

 

A

請參考[新開通識課程申請作業流程](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/download/flowProcess/file/Gedu/Geduflow4.pdf)。

Q

          核心通識與一般通識有何差別？        

展開
收合

 

A

一、課程設計不同：核心通識課程由系所負責規劃並制訂共同課綱，一門核心通識課程可能由多位不同教師開班，但每位教師的授課內容至少會有70%與共同課綱相同。3學分的課程包含2小時正課及1小時討論課。

二、教學方式不同：核心通識課程之規劃以培養學生具備宏觀思維、自學能力、獨立思維、公民意識等知能為原則，透過大班教學、小組討論的方式進行，每門課均有教學助理（TA）協助帶領議題討論。

 

自主學習 常見問題
 

Q

          自主學習書院通識課程是什麼？        

展開
收合

 

A

為發展書院通識特色課程，培養學生自主學習、問題解決及跨領域實作等綜合能力，提供學生主動規劃發展課程之機會，建立師生共學校園文化，依申請方式分為「開課型」及「認證型」二類自主學習。

Q

          「開課型」及「認證型」二類自主學習有什麼不同？        

展開
收合

 

A

「開課型」自主學習課程指學習內容與方式由學生自主規劃，或師生共同規劃設計之課程，比照新開通識課程申請開課；「認證型」自主學習則是為鼓勵學生發展問題解決和創新實踐能力，得經相關領域教師輔導或獨立完成學習計畫，學習場域不限於校內。

Q

          如何申請開課？        

展開
收合

 

A

填寫募課申請書及新開通識申請表，並檢附籌備會議紀錄送交通識教育中心， 另請留意後續會議審查時需派代表到場說明。每年 3 月、10 月受理開課申請，截止日期請留意教務處網頁公告，或可洽詢通識教育中心承辦人。

Q

          每門課程學分數是多少？        

展開
收合

 

A

每門課程學分數為一至二學分，由師生共同規劃決定。

Q

          開課是否有人數限制？        

展開
收合

 

A

一人即可提出申請，通過後列入選課系統開放全校同學選課，選課人數達七 人方可成功開課。

Q

          如何申請認證？        

展開
收合

 

A

採事先登記，事後認證。事先填寫[Google 表單](https://forms.gle/kQB3AH7JRmNYhPkr7)報備，於學習計畫完成後進行成果發表並檢具學習檔案，每年 3 月、10 月受理學分認證申請，截止日期請留意教務處網頁公告，或可洽詢通識教育中心承辦人。

Q

          申請認證通識學分有哪些條件？        

展開
收合

 

A

認證以一學分為基本單位，採計上限二學分，申請認證須進行成果發表並檢 具學習檔案。成果發表可以選擇自行公開發表，或參加通識中心自主學習期 末聯合成果展；學習檔案則須包含以下四點：學習目標、方法與過程、成果 及個人反思，並檢附佐證資料。

Q

          課程師資來源為何？        

展開
收合

 

A

課程需邀請本校專兼任教師或具教師資格之專任研究人員擔任開課教師，另得視需要邀請校外教師、業師指導，指導時數與方式需有指導紀錄供本中心備查。

Q

          成績如何計算？        

展開
收合

 

A

依本校相關規定採「通過或不通過」或「等第制」，可由師生討論議定；惟「自 主學習」課程完成後，需進行成果發表並提交成果報告，成果報告須集結成 一份「學習歷程檔案」，成果形式可以為文件、相片、影音、表演、展覽、設 計成品等。

Q

          規劃認證型自主學習計畫有哪些注意事項？        

展開
收合

 

A

認證型自主學習分為社會實踐類、學術探索類及創新實作類，不限制其方式、 場域及時程，可以參與校內外各式計畫，也可以是課程所學的延伸，亦或是你有興趣深入學習的主題，每個學習規劃以 2 人以上為原則。若你想執行認證型自主學習，建議可以先與校內教師（或班級導師）商談討論，也有利於後續順利進行喔！

Q

          學習過程中需要協助，該怎麼辦？        

展開
收合

 

A

有任何問題，都可以與指導教師或通識中心商談。如有需要，通識中心也可代為宣傳方便找到合適的夥伴共同執行，或尋找各項資源之訊息。

Q

          可以半途放棄嗎？        

展開
收合

 

A

如無法完成課程，請依照一般課程棄修規定辦理。

Q

          課程中若有安排校外教師、業師指導或安排演講等需要，相關費用如何支應？        

展開
收合

 

A

每門課程預算上限以教授授課鐘點費乘以學分數乘以上課週數計，經費運用 由師生共同討論議定。詳細規定請見[國立政治大學自主學習書院通識課程實施要點](https://nccuooa.app.huhu.tw/download/rulesdata/law115A.pdf)。

title: faq
text:
FAQ

    FAQs  

 

Students FAQs
 

Summer General Education Courses
 

Q

          What summer courses are available?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

In addition to summer courses offered by NCCU based on student demand (For the schedule and detailed regulations, please refer to the [Office of Academic Affairs website](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/zh/%E6%9C%8D%E5%8B%99%E9%A0%85%E7%9B%AE/%E9%81%B8%E8%AA%B2/%E6%9A%91%E4%BF%AE) or contact the Office of Registration.), students may also select courses from the [Summer College](https://www.n2.org.tw/) and [SOS Online School](https://www.ewant.org/local/enterprise/collegepage.php?id=5). Some of these courses may be recognized as general education credits. Students must follow the “[Summer Academy General Education Course Implementation Guidelines and Registration Instructions](https://www.n2.org.tw/enter/document_introduce/2).” Tuition is self-paid (discounts available for incoming freshmen and undergraduate students at partner schools; graduate students pay full tuition). Grades are recorded according to the University’s summer course regulations.

Q

          Who is eligible to take winter or summer general education courses?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

Only currently enrolled NCCU students. Incoming freshmen may also enroll in the National Summer College or SOS Online Summer Academy for summer courses, using their admission proof but must apply for credit recognition at the Center for General Education by October 30 of the same year. For approved courses, only the course title and credits will be recorded; the grade will not be included.

Q

          What is the maximum number of general education credits from the National Summer College and SOS Online Summer Academy that NCCU will recognize?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

According to school regulations, the recognition limit is 6 credits per semester.

Q

          Is there a course limit for taking general education courses during off-campus summer sessions?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

3 Courses for the Summer College; 4 credits for the SOS! online Summer Academy. 

Q

          I am missing two credits in a specific general education category to graduate. Can I take summer courses and apply for recognition?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

Yes. For NCCU summer courses, refer to Q14 and contact the Office of Registration. For the National Summer College or SOS Online Summer Academy, check the NCCU-recognized courses on the official website, complete course selection, payment, and attendance, and then submit a credit recognition application to the Center for General Education.

Q

          I want to take courses out of personal interest and do not wish to apply for credit recognition. Can I take courses not recognized by NCCU?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

 Yes. However, courses not recognized by NCCU will not have grades recorded in the system.

Q

          I am currently on a leave of absence. Can I enroll in summer general education courses?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

No, you must first resume your enrollment. Only students with proof of active enrollment can complete the registration process online and proceed with course selection, payment, and course attendance.

National Summer College: [https://www.n2.org.tw/](https://www.n2.org.tw/)

SOS Online Summer Academy: [https://www.ewant.org/local/enterprise/collegepage.php?id=5](https://www.ewant.org/local/enterprise/collegepage.php?id=5)

General Education Center Summer Course Guide: [https://www.facebook.com/photo?fbid=1061207776056865&set=pcb.1061212512723058](https://www.facebook.com/photo?fbid=1061207776056865&set=pcb.1061212512723058)For detailed regulations, contact Ms. Chang at the General Education Center (ext. 63871).

Q

          How are summer course grades calculated? Will they affect my GPA or ranking?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

Grades are recorded in the third semester for on-campus summer courses or the fourth semester for the National Summer College and SOS Online Summer Academy. They are not included in the GPA calculation for the first and second semesters, so they do not affect your GPA but will count toward your graduation ranking.

 

General Education Credit Transfer for Domestic and International Exchange Programs
 

Q

          What is the maximum limit for overseas credit transfer?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

For undergraduate programs, the transferred credits may not exceed one-third of the minimum credits required for graduation. For master’s and doctoral programs, the limit is one-half of the minimum graduation credits. For students pursuing a dual degree abroad, the transferred credits may not exceed two-thirds of the minimum credits required for graduation.

Q

          Can courses taken at a domestic exchange university be used to transfer general education credits? Which courses are eligible?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

Credit transfer for general education is limited to general education courses taken at the exchange university. Only Language general education, Common general education, and College general education courses are eligible for transfer. Core general education courses are not eligible for credit transfer.

Q

          Must I return to Taiwan to apply for overseas credit transfer? Can I confirm in advance whether overseas credits can be successfully transferred before going abroad?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

Since credit transfer reviews are conducted based on the similarity between the syllabus of the overseas course and that of NCCU’s general education courses, it is not possible to confirm in advance whether the credits can be successfully transferred before departure. If students wish to seek prior confirmation, they may contact the Center for General Education by email during the course selection period of their overseas exchange. When sending the inquiry, please attach both the syllabus of the NCCU general education course for which credit transfer is sought and the syllabus of the overseas course with similar content, so that the Center for General Education conduct a preliminary review.

If the result of the preliminary review indicates that the credits are transferable, students must still complete the course during the exchange period and obtain a passing grade. Upon formally applying after the exchange, students must submit their transcript and relevant documents in order for the credits to be transferred. For detailed application procedures, please refer to Credit Transfer of Overseas Exchange Credits to NCCU General Education Credits.

Q

          Can I use courses taken at a domestic or overseas exchange school to fulfill the University’s general education requirements?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

According to the [Regulations on NCCU Students Taking Courses Abroad](https://oic.nccu.edu.tw/Upload/FileManager/4fd69618-9214-4e09-8d0d-fedd22618293.pdf), after your exchange semester ends, you may submit your official transcript or proof of grades from the exchange school and apply for credit transfer by the one-third mark of the following semester. You need to search in the University’s course database for general education courses with the same or similar course title or syllabus (note: core and college-level general education courses cannot be used for this transfer). The course must be offered during the semester of your exchange, but general education courses within ten years of that year are also eligible. For transferable courses and credits, please refer to Article 6 of the University’s Student Credit Transfer Regulations. Once your application is approved by the General Education Center, the courses taken at the exchange school can be credited as the University’s general education courses.

Q

          What is the procedure for applying to transfer general education credits from domestic or overseas exchanges?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

1. Based on the syllabus of the foreign school, search in the University’s course database for general education courses with the same or similar course title or syllabus. During the review, credit transfer will be judged based on syllabus similarity.

2. Prepare a copy of your transcript from the foreign school (stamped “certified true copy” by the Office of International Cooperation or your department), the syllabus of the course(s) you wish to transfer, and the corresponding NCCU course syllabus. Submit these materials along with the application form to the General Education Center within the designated period. For detailed regulations, please refer to the NCCU Student Credit Transfer Regulations.

 

Department Transfer / Switching Double Major to Single Major
 

Q

          After transferring departments, or adding a double major or minor, I found that some general education courses I previously took are now excluded for students in my current program. Can these still count toward my graduation general education credits? Also, if I transfer to a department exempt from the Information Literacy requirement, can the previously completed Information Literacy credits still count?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

According to [Article 6 of the University’s](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/download/rulesdata/law12A.pdf)[Regulations on Double Majors and Minors](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/download/rulesdata/law12A.pdf): courses taken before obtaining eligibility for a double major or minor, even if they are excluded for students in the new program, will still be counted toward graduation general education credits. Previously completed Information Literacy credits will be retained and can count toward graduation credits. Conversely, if you transfer from a department exempt from Information Literacy to one that requires it, you must make up the required credits.

Q

          Regarding the maximum number of general education credits that can be recognized across different combinations, if I have a minor and also a credit program, how many general education credits can be recognized?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

The total number of recognized credits across all categories is capped at 9 credits. Please refer to [the National Chengchi University General Education Credit Recognition Guidelines.](https://gecenter.nccu.edu.tw/wp-content/uploads/law117A.pdf)

Q

          I was originally in Department A, then added Department B as a double major and plan to graduate from Department B, while my original department becomes a minor. How can I apply for recognition of general education credits?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

You must first apply at the Registration Office for “Double Major to Primary Major” status. Then, you can use courses from your original Department A (now a minor) for general education credit recognition. Please note that if you want to change your original department to a minor, you must complete at least two-thirds of the required minor credits to be eligible. For detailed rules, please refer to [the University’s](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/download/rulesdata/law12A.pdf)regulations on double majors and minors.

Q

          I was originally in Department A, then transferred to Department B and plan to graduate from Department B. Can I use the required courses from Department A to fulfill my general education credits?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

No. If you wish to use Department A’s required courses to fulfill general education credits, you must first apply to have Department A as a double major or minor. Then review the required [courses table for the double major or minor](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/zh/%E6%9C%8D%E5%8B%99%E9%A0%85%E7%9B%AE/%E8%AA%B2%E7%A8%8B%E7%9B%B8%E9%97%9C%E8%B3%87%E8%A8%8A/%E5%BF%85%E4%BF%AE%E7%A7%91%E7%9B%AE%E8%A1%A8%E6%9F%A5%E8%A9%A22), as well as the[general education categories recognized for the double major or minor](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/18f7nhWsJnKl-QkFAatBIXvbBjRqzcBRC). Use the required and elective courses listed in the table to determine the corresponding general education credits.

 

General Education Credit Recognition / Exemption
 

Q

          If I plan to extend my studies by one semester or one year to participate in a domestic or overseas exchange program, can I apply in advance for credit recognition for a double major, minor, or credit program?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

You may apply after returning to campus or to Taiwan, or you may authorize someone else to apply on your behalf. When authorizing another person to apply, you must submit the [Power of Attorney for Applying for Various Certification Documentsissued by the Registration Section, Office of Academic Affairs, National Chengchi University](https://diplomacy.nccu.edu.tw/upload/28/doc/3092/44_3372%20(1).pdf).

Q

          Why is it recommended to apply for general education credit recognition during the graduation semester? Is it possible to apply earlier?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

Once the application is submitted, it cannot be modified. To protect students’ rights and interests, it is recommended that students confirm their entire credit plan before applying during the graduation semester.

Q

          Which courses from double majors, minors, or credit programs can be recognized for general education credit?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

Please refer to the required course lists for your double major, minor, or credit program, and only courses listed there are eligible for recognition. 

[Query double major/minor required courses](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1vCUjZmLK-E3oNLUeO14tkwUJgy4jUdXA/view?usp=sharing)

 

Q

          Which courses from double majors, minors, or credit programs can be recognized for general education credit?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

 Please refer to the required course lists for your double major, minor, or credit program, and only courses listed there are eligible for recognition. [Query double major/minor required courses](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/18f7nhWsJnKl-QkFAatBIXvbBjRqzcBRC)

Q

          If I use courses from my double major, minor, or credit program for recognition, will the credits counted as elective or required for my major/minor/credit program be deducted, potentially affecting my qualification?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

No. Courses from a double major, minor, or credit program used for recognition will count as general education credits for graduation purposes, but they do not affect your qualification or degree for the double major, minor, or credit program. As long as you have completed the required courses for these programs, you remain qualified. Only the credit category changes from “major/required” to “general education.” Please ensure that your remaining major/required credits meet graduation requirements.

Q

          What should I pay attention to when applying?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

1.Once submitted, applications cannot be changed. It is strongly recommended to apply during your intended graduation semester.

2.Confirm the number of general education credits you have already earned, check which categories your double major, minor, or credit program courses can be recognized under, and then download the application form online or obtain it from the General Education Center and submit it.

3.Once recognized courses are approved and recorded, no further changes may be made.

 

Other Issues
 

Q

          What should I do if I realize I am missing general education credits before graduation?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

First, check which general education category credits are missing.

If you are eligible and have taken courses in your double major, minor, or credit program, you can apply to have those courses recognized under the corresponding general education category.

If the course category does not match or you do not have eligibility, you can enroll in summer courses, including:

Summer courses offered by the University (for details, please refer to the bachelor summer course registration procedures or contact the Office of the Registrar).

Inter-university summer general education courses (e.g., SOS! Summer Online Academy, National Summer College, the courses approved for credit recognition by the University). For more details, please refer to the summer course information.

Q

          Can an interdisciplinary general education course count toward two different categories at the same time?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

No. Interdisciplinary general education courses can only be recognized under a single category. During your study period, the course may appear under either of the two relevant categories in the academic system. At graduation, the course will generally be counted toward the category in which you have fewer credits.

Example: If you take an interdisciplinary course covering both social and humanities domains, the system may display it as either “Humanities” or “Social Sciences” while you are enrolled. When calculating graduation credits, if your Social Sciences credits are fewer than Humanities credits, the course will be counted as a Social Sciences credit. If you need to request a change in the recognized category, please contact the Office of the Registration.

Q

          How can I apply to have Chinese or foreign language general education credits recognized?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

For Chinese general education credits, please contact the[Department of Chinese](https://chinese.nccu.edu.tw/PageDocAll?fid=1890). For foreign language general education credits, please contact the [Foreign Languages Center](https://flc.nccu.edu.tw/).

 

Teachers FAQs
 

Course Offering Issues
 

Q

          Are there resources or funding available for offering GE courses, such as TAs or budgets?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

Currently, only core GE courses provide TAs and course funding. Other general GE courses may apply for funding based on course type and enrollment. Self-directed learning college GE courses have corresponding funding support. Additionally, courses that meet the criteria for the Office of Academic Affairs’ teaching innovation grants may apply for funding, but courses that have already received support from other units in the same semester are not eligible for duplicate funding.

For more details, please see [Course Subsidy](https://gecenter.nccu.edu.tw/en/faculty-zone/course-subsidy/).

Q

          What kinds of courses require re-approval?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

1.Course modifications, including: adding/changing instructors, adding/changing the offering department, adding sections, modifying excluded departments, changing course title, syllabus, or credit hours.

2.Courses that have not been offered for more than three years. (Core GE courses are exempt from this rule.)

Q

          How can I apply to offer a General Education course?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

Please refer to[the](https://aca.nccu.edu.tw/download/flowProcess/file/Gedu/Geduflow4.pdf)procedure for proposing a new General Education course.

(1) Language and Humanities General Courses: Ms. Wu, Ext. 63872, Email: yun63872@nccu.edu.tw

(2) Social Sciences Courses: Mr. Hsiao, Ext. 62856, Email: yuanchao@nccu.edu.tw

(3) Natural Sciences Courses: Ms. Chang, Ext. 62847, Email: changwc@nccu.edu.tw

(4) Technology and Informatics Courses: Ms. Lin, Ext. 62857, Email: jeanlin@nccu.edu.tw

(5) College General Education Courses : Ms. Chang, Ext. 63871, Email: chy@nccu.edu.tw

Q

          What is the difference between Core General Education and General Education courses?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

1.Course design: Core GE courses are planned by the department with a common syllabus. A single core GE course may be taught by multiple instructors, but at least 70% of each instructor’s content must follow the common syllabus. A 3-credit course includes 2 hours of lecture and 1 hour of discussion.

2.Teaching approach: Core GE courses aim to develop students’ macro-level thinking, self-learning ability, independent thinking, and civic awareness. Classes use a combination of large lectures and small group discussions, with teaching assistants (TAs) supporting the discussion sessions.

 

Self-Directed Learning FAQs
 

Q

          What are Self-Directed Learning College GE courses?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

These courses are designed to develop the unique characteristics of the College’s GE curriculum, fostering students’ self-directed learning, problem-solving, and interdisciplinary practical skills. They provide students with opportunities to proactively plan and develop courses while promoting a culture of co-learning between faculty and students. Self-directed learning is divided into two types based on the application method: “Course-Based” and “Certification-Based.”

Q

          What is the difference between the “Course-Based” and “Certification-Based” self-directed learning types?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

1.Course-Based: The course content and learning methods are planned by students independently or jointly with faculty. These courses follow the same procedure as applying for a newly proposed GE course.

2.Certification-Based: These courses aim to encourage students to develop problem-solving and innovative practical skills. Students may be guided by faculty in the relevant field or complete a learning plan independently. The learning environment is not limited to on-campus settings.

Q

          How do I apply to offer a course?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

Complete the Course Proposal Application and the New GE Course Application Form, and submit them along with the preparatory meeting minutes to the Center for General Education. Please note that a representative must attend the subsequent review meeting to provide explanations. Applications are accepted in March and October each year. Check the Office of Academic Affairs website for deadlines, or contact Ms.Chang in the Center for General Education. ( Mailbox: chy@nccu.edu.tw)

 

Q

          How many credits does each course carry?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

Each course carries 1–2 credits, determined jointly by the students and instructor.

Q

          Is there a minimum number of students required?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

Only one student is needed to propose a course. Once approved, the course will be listed in the registration system for all students to select. A minimum of seven students must enroll for the course to officially run.

Q

          How do I apply for accreditation?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

 The process is pre-registration followed by accreditation. You must first report your plan through a [Google Form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeoB9QdRYk5nYsT3HkffWS2k3MX1JaI2edwMdyqIOIbEXoK8A/viewform). After completing your learning project, you are required to present your results and submit learning documentation. Applications for credit accreditation are accepted each March and October. Please pay attention to the deadlines announced on the Office of Academic Affairs website, or consult the Center for General Education for details.

Q

          What are the requirements for applying for general education credit accreditation?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

Accreditation is based on one credit as the basic unit, with a maximum of two credits. To apply for accreditation, you must present results and submit learning documentation. The result presentation can either be a public presentation organized by the students themselves or participation in the Center fpr General Education ’s joint final result exhibition. The learning documentation must include the following four elements: learning objectives, methods and process, results , and personal reflection, along with supporting evidence.

Q

          Who can serve as instructors?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

Courses must be taught by full-time or part-time NCCU faculty or qualified research staff. External instructors or industry professionals may also be invited, with all guidance hours and methods documented for the Center for General Education.

Q

          How are grades calculated?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

Grades follow the University’s regulations and may be Pass/Fail or letter-graded, as decided by the instructor and students. Upon completion, students must present their outcomes and submit a Learning Portfolio. The portfolio may include documents, photos, videos, performances, exhibitions, or design products.

Q

          What should I keep in mind when planning an accredited self-directed learning project?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

Accredited self-directed learning is divided into three categories: social practice, academic exploration, and innovative implementation. There are no restrictions on methods, venues, or timeframes. Projects may involve participation in various on- or off-campus programs, extensions of what you have learned in courses, or subjects you wish to explore in greater depth. Each project must involve at least two participants. If you plan to carry out an accredited self-directed learning project, it is recommended that you first consult with a faculty member (or your class advisor), which will also facilitate smoother progress later on.

Q

          What if I need assistance during the learning process?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

For any questions, you may consult your supervising faculty member or the General Education Center. If needed, the General Education Center can also help promote your project to find suitable partners, or provide information about various available resources.

Q

          Can students withdraw midway?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

If unable to complete the course, follow the standard course withdrawal procedures.

Q

          If the course includes guest lectures, guidance from external instructors, or industry professionals, how should the related expenses be covered?        

Expand
Collapse

 

A

The maximum budget for each course is calculated based on the instructor’s hourly pay rate multiplied by the number of credits and the number of teaching weeks. The use of funds should be jointly discussed and decided by both the instructor and the students.

For detailed regulations, please refer to the [Guidelines for the Implementation of the General Education Courses of the College of Self-directed Learning, National Chengchi University](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1z80qihVOvIgPC3h16thuf_3jX4O22gws/view?usp=sharing).

title: qa21
text: These courses are designed to develop the unique characteristics of the College’s GE curriculum, fostering students’ self-directed learning, problem-solving, and interdisciplinary practical skills. They provide students with opportunities to proactively plan and develop courses while promoting a culture of co-learning between faculty and students. Self-directed learning is divided into two types based on the application method: “Course-Based” and “Certification-Based.”

title: qa11
text: Accreditation is based on one credit as the basic unit, with a maximum of two credits. To apply for accreditation, you must present results and submit learning documentation. The result presentation can either be a public presentation organized by the students themselves or participation in the Center fpr General Education ’s joint final result exhibition. The learning documentation must include the following four elements: learning objectives, methods and process, results , and personal reflection, along with supporting evidence.

title: qa12
text: Accredited self-directed learning is divided into three categories: social practice, academic exploration, and innovative implementation. There are no restrictions on methods, venues, or timeframes. Projects may involve participation in various on- or off-campus programs, extensions of what you have learned in courses, or subjects you wish to explore in greater depth. Each project must involve at least two participants. If you plan to carry out an accredited self-directed learning project, it is recommended that you first consult with a faculty member (or your class advisor), which will also facilitate smoother progress later on.

title: qa13
text: The process is pre-registration followed by accreditation. After completing your learning project, you are required to present your results and submit learning documentation. Applications for credit accreditation are accepted each March and October. During your study period, the course may appear under either of the two relevant categories in the academic system. At graduation, the course will generally be counted toward the category in which you have fewer credits.

Example: If you take an interdisciplinary course covering both social and humanities domains, the system may display it as either “Humanities” or “Social Sciences” while you are enrolled. When authorizing another person to apply, you must submit the [Power of Attorney for Applying for Various Certification Documentsissued by the Registration Section, Office of Academic Affairs, National Chengchi University](https://diplomacy.nccu.edu.tw/upload/28/doc/3092/44_3372%20(1).pdf).

title: must-i-return-to-taiwan-to-apply-for-overseas-credit-transfer-can-i-confirm-in-advance-whether-overseas-credits-can-be-successfully-transferred-before-going-abroad
text:
Since credit transfer reviews are conducted based on the similarity between the syllabus of the overseas course and that of NCCU’s general education courses, it is not possible to confirm in advance whether the credits can be successfully transferred before departure. If students wish to seek prior confirmation, they may contact the Center for General Education by email during the course selection period of their overseas exchange. When sending the inquiry, please attach both the syllabus of the NCCU general education course for which credit transfer is sought and the syllabus of the overseas course with similar content, so that the Center for General Education conduct a preliminary review.

If the result of the preliminary review indicates that the credits are transferable, students must still complete the course during the exchange period and obtain a passing grade. Upon formally applying after the exchange, students must submit their transcript and relevant documents in order for the credits to be transferred. For detailed application procedures, please refer to Credit Transfer of Overseas Exchange Credits to NCCU General Education Credits.

title: can-courses-taken-at-a-domestic-exchange-university-be-used-to-transfer-general-education-credits-which-courses-are-eligible
